name: Silas/Silvanus
title: Paul's faithful missionary companion
summary: Silas, also known as Silvanus, was a leading figure in the early church in Jerusalem and became Paul's most important co-worker on his second missionary journey. He was a Roman citizen and prophet who played a central role in bringing the gospel to Europe and was a co-author of several New Testament letters.

keyEvents.title: Sent from Jerusalem with the apostolic letter
keyEvents.description: Silas was chosen as a leading man in the Jerusalem church to bring the decision of the apostles' council to Gentile Christians in Antioch, together with Judas Barsabbas.

keyEvents.title: Joins Paul on the second missionary journey
keyEvents.description: After Paul and Barnabas parted ways, Paul chose Silas as his new travel companion for the missionary journey through Syria and Cilicia.

keyEvents.title: Imprisoned in Philippi
keyEvents.description: Paul and Silas were beaten and thrown into prison in Philippi, but in the middle of the night they sang hymns, an earthquake opened the doors, and the jailer and his household were saved.

keyEvents.title: Persecution in Thessalonica and Berea
keyEvents.description: Silas accompanied Paul to Thessalonica and Berea where they preached in the synagogues, but had to flee due to persecution from Jewish opponents.

keyEvents.title: Ministry in Corinth
keyEvents.description: Silas and Timothy joined Paul in Corinth, where together they proclaimed the gospel and established the church there.

keyEvents.title: Co-author of letters
keyEvents.description: Silvanus is mentioned as a co-author of the letters to the Thessalonians, and later he helped Peter write his first letter.
